Free Apple ID signing typically expires after 7 days. When the app won't open after expiration, reconnect the iPhone and press `Cmd + R` in Xcode to reinstall and renew the signing for 7 more days:

```bash
cd /Users/max/Desktop/github/interview
source ~/.nvm/nvm.sh && nvm use 22
npx cap open ios
```

If you're only renewing the signing without changing content, you don't need to rebuild the web artifacts.

```bash
cd /Users/max/Desktop/github/interview
```

aldinelabs/pine.body:
# Pine

An AI agent workspace dedicated to providing more possibilities for everyone.

> [!CAUTION]
> Pine is currently an early developer preview. Its interface, data formats, and Agent behavior may all undergo incompatible changes. Do not use it for important data.

## Introduction

Most AI Agent tools are aimed at developers: terminals, editor plugins, command-line arguments. Pine is a desktop Agent workspace for people who work with documents, spreadsheets, reports, and materials every day:

- Various files can be previewed directly within the workspace, so the Agent operates on the files you see.
- The Agent's reads, tool calls, and file modifications are all shown in the session. Operations that require approval ask first, and you can abort at any time.
- Projects, sessions, and files are saved on your local machine. Model connections (API key / OAuth) are configured by you; Pine does not act as a relay.

## Features

- Sessions are organized by project. One project can link to multiple folders, each with read-only or read-write permissions set separately. Multiple sessions can run at the same time.
- Preview of text and code, PDF, Office / iWork documents, data spreadsheets, images, audio and video, archives, email, e-books, charts, CAD drawings, 3D models, and more.
- The Agent's local tools are restricted to authorized folders, with multiple permission modes ranging from approving each action individually to fully autonomous.
- Task lists, background processes, context compression, image generation, and web search and fetching.
- Supports Skills, MCP servers, and Computer Use.
- Includes built-in models from multiple providers; custom providers and models can also be added.
- Use Pine in a browser, or pair other devices via QR code / link to remotely use the Pine on this computer through Aldine. No port forwarding is needed, and the connection is end-to-end encrypted (Settings → Remote Control).
- Chinese and English interface, light / dark themes, and optional reading fonts.

macOS is supported. Windows is partially supported. Linux is not yet supported.

## Running from Source

Requires [Bun](https://bun.sh/). See the `packageManager` field in `package.json` for the specific version.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/aldinelabs/pine.git
cd pine
bun install --frozen-lockfile
bun run dev
```

On first launch on Windows, you will be prompted to configure the Windows sandbox. Follow the prompts and allow it in UAC.

## Server Deployment

Pine can also run without a window on a macOS or Linux server, and be used only through a browser. It requires a relatively recent Node.js; Linux also requires bubblewrap, socat, and ripgrep. See the deployment documentation for specific requirements:

```bash
bun install --frozen-lockfile
bun run build:server
PINE_PASSWORD='at least 8 characters' node…
```

dalinaum/rs.body:
# Dalinaum's KOSPI Relative Strength Rating

We built a site based on [William O'Neil's Relative Strength Rating](https://www.williamoneil.com/proprietary-ratings-and-rankings/).

 * [Dalinaum's KOSPI Relative Strength](https://dalinaum.github.io/rs/)

The site is scheduled to update automatically with the KOSPI relative strength around 4 PM, Monday through Friday. If it isn't updated by 4:30 PM, there is a system error.

## William O'Neil's Relative Strength Rating

William O'Neil's site describes the calculation method as follows.

RELATIVE STRENGTH RATING

This technical tool is one of the most popular ways for clients to see the market's top performers. The Relative Strength Rating is the result of calculating a stock's percentage price change over the last 12 months. A 40% weight is assigned to the latest three-month period; the remaining three quarters each receive 20% weight. All stocks are arranged in order of greatest price percentage change and assigned a percentile rank from 99 (highest) to 1 (lowest).

## How This Site Calculates It

Following O'Neil's description, we calculated the price change for each of the four quarters, counted only the most recent quarter at double weight with the rest weighted equally, and ranked the stocks. To spread scores evenly, the top-ranked stock gets 99 points and the bottom-ranked stock gets 1 point.

For more details on the calculation method...

# Open People Input (OPI)

The Chinese name is **小欧** (also the project's pet), and the English name is **opi**. The input method is officially called **小欧输入法** (opi input method also works).

## A multi-platform input method that returns to its essentials and is usable by everyone

> **Want to install it on your own machine?** Installation guides for each platform are in **[`docs/install/`](https://github.com/erikwang2013/opi/blob/HEAD/docs/install/README.md)** (build / package / install / usage, split by platform).
> **One more step is required after installing**: **add OPI to the input method group**. A newly installed input method is not enabled automatically. Without this step, it appears in the input method list but nothing happens when you type. (The fcitx5 plugin reload is already done automatically by the install script.)
> For step-by-step commands, see §4 of [`docs/install/linux.md`](https://github.com/erikwang2013/opi/blob/HEAD/docs/install/linux.md).

> **Website**: [https://opi.erik.xyz](https://opi.erik.xyz) (source: [`site/index.html`](https://github.com/erikwang2013/opi/blob/HEAD/site/index.html)). It includes a full-screen scrolling project introduction, a 3D keycap environment with a first-visit memory timeline, feature iterations, the complete version changelog, and downloads for each platform. The donation QR code opens in place, and the footer contains the filing number.
>
> **Verification boundary**: which layers have been verified on each platform, and which have not yet been tested on real hardware, is determined uniformly by the corresponding sections of [`docs/install/`](https://github.com/erikwang2013/opi/blob/HEAD/docs/install/README.md).
>

### 🐾 Meet Xiao Ou

**Xiao Ou** is OPI's project pet, a **keycap sprite**.

It looks exactly like a key on a keyboard, because an input method should be just that. It doesn't need to be anything else.

| On its body | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **Body = keycap** | The body of the input. It doesn't steal the spotlight and does just one small thing |
| **Mouth = letter O** | Open: open source, open, auditable |
| **Antenna on top = pinyin tone mark ˉ** | Pinyin input. Cinnabar red, the only warm color on its whole body |

kan/pike.body:
# Pike

**A lightweight development environment specialized for "AI agents × terminal".** It aims to be a substitute for VS Code for developers who work mainly in the terminal.

Built with Tauri v2 (Rust + Vue / TypeScript). It primarily targets Windows. The macOS (Apple Silicon) build is also signed, notarized, and distributed, and auto-update works the same way. On macOS, you can develop using the host's login shell. Only Windows-specific features (WSL, jump lists, administrator terminal, window background transparency) are not supported.

## Main features

- **Multi-terminal**: xterm.js + PTY (WSL / cmd / PowerShell / PowerShell 7 / Git Bash; login shell on macOS), shell selection from the taskbar and tray menu
- **AI agents**: Designed for running Claude Code / Codex / Copilot CLI / opencode directly in the terminal. Launch buttons shown only for installed agents, resuming past sessions, inserting prompt templates, and notifications when an agent is waiting for input
- **Agent status**: Check account, usage rate, token usage, and cost for each agent in use. Follows multiple accounts (`CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`) and can receive the actual account from Claude Code hooks
- **AI assistance in the terminal**: Click paths in output to open files, images, or directories (with or without line numbers). Send editor selections, line references, diagnostics, and instructions to start working on an issue to the terminal
- **Editor**: CodeMirror 6 (30+ languages), minimap, search and replace, git diff gutter, conflict resolution, go-to-definition, per-tab word wrap toggle, character encoding and line ending support
- **Markdown input assistance**: Toolbar for inserting syntax, templates for tables and footnotes, image insertion (select, paste, drop), and conversion of pasted URLs into links with the page title
- **Browser tabs**: Open external pages such as Jira or GitHub in tabs. Keeps login state and restores tabs after restart

molimao/iota.body:
# IOTA Watch

An open-source, five-language, multi-project monitoring dashboard centered on **IOTA Train at Home**. It supports IOTA, XID / MMM, Quantus, fly.ai, Nosana, Gonka, Akash, io.net, Vast.ai and Golem; each project's inputs, cycles, and data coverage are described separately.

**[Official site](https://iotahome.site) · [My Devices](https://iotahome.site/zh/devices) · [IOTA Lookup](https://iotahome.site/zh/app) · [Network Status](https://iotahome.site/zh/network) · [Blog](https://iotahome.site/zh/blog) · [English](https://iotahome.site/en)**

IOTA Watch is an independent MIT-licensed monitor in English, Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese, Korean and Japanese. IOTA Train at Home (Macrocosmos / Bittensor SN9) is the core project, with ten project pages covering training, mining and compute. Tool pages query records; separate tutorials explain identifiers, fields and troubleshooting. Public projects use public identifiers; io.net and Vast.ai require account connections with read credentials. Those two integrations have mocked validation; real-account validation remains pending.

The screenshot shows miner distribution and network capacity; the figures are official data as of when the screenshot was taken.

## Features

- **Multi-device monitoring**: add, name, and view devices by public Miner ID, filtering by contributing, waiting for tasks, needs checking, and pending confirmation.
- **Earnings records**: today, cumulative, paid, pending payment, frozen, and minimum payment amounts; also shows USD valuations with source and timestamp.
- **Training history**: view training tokens, throughput, and cumulative tokens by day, week, or month; missing data is left as gaps.
- **Network visualization**: regional distribution donut chart, miner count rankings, slot occupancy, task progress, and tier overview.

# Konke Smart for Home Assistant

This project is a Konke Smart integration developed for the latest version of Home Assistant. Its goal is to bridge devices already saved in the Konke Smart app to Home Assistant, so they can work with devices from other brands and enable some automations.

## Installation

### Method 1: One-click installation

Run the following in the Home Assistant Terminal / SSH:

```bash
curl --retry 3 --retry-all-errors --connect-timeout 15 --max-time 120 -fsSL --http1.1 https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sjhshebe/konke-homeassistant/main/install.sh -o /tmp/konke-install.sh && sh /tmp/konke-install.sh
```

The script downloads `konke.zip` from the latest GitHub Release and installs it to `custom_components/konke` in Home Assistant. After installation, Home Assistant Core restarts automatically.

To install a specific version, set `KONKE_VERSION`:

```bash
curl --retry 3 --retry-all-errors --connect-timeout 15 --max-time 120 -fsSL --http1.1 https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sjhshebe/konke-homeassistant/main/install.sh -o /tmp/konke-install.sh && KONKE_VERSION=v0.8.1 sh /tmp/konke-install.sh
```

If your environment does not have `curl`, you can use:

```bash
wget -q -T 30 -t 3 https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sjhshebe/konke-homeassistant/main/install.sh -O /tmp/konke-install.sh && sh /tmp/konke-install.sh
```
